en.title: I Love to Tell the Story
en.author: A. Katherine Hankey
stanzas:
[G]I love to tell the story
Of un[C]seen things a[G]bove,
Of [D7]Jesus and His [G]glory,
Of Jesus and His [D7]love.
[D]I love to [G]tell the [D7]story,
Be[Em]cause I know ’tis [B7]true;
It [C]satisfies my [G]longings
As [D7]nothing else can [G]do.

I love to tell the story;
More wonderful it seems
Than all the golden fancies
Of all our golden dreams.
I love to tell the story,
It did so much for me;
And that is just the reason
I tell it now to thee.

I love to tell the story;
’Tis pleasant to repeat
What seems, each time I tell it,
More wonderfully sweet.
I love to tell the story,
For some have never heard
The message of salvation
From God’s own holy Word.

I love to tell the story,
For those who know it best
Seem hungering and thirsting
To hear it like the rest.
And when, in scenes of glory,
I sing the new, new song,
’Twill be the old, old story
That I have loved so long.
en.chorus:
[G]I [D]love to tell the [G]story,
’Twill [C]be my theme in [G]glory,
To tell the old, [D7]old [G]story
[C]Of Jesus and [D7]His [G]love.

notes: Text: Cyber Hymnal (Hankey's 1866 poem 'The Story Told'); four stanzas, the standard printed set. Timeless Truths gives two wording variants — 'as nothing else would do' (st. 1) and 'What seems each time I tell it' unpunctuated (st. 3); the Cyber Hymnal readings used here match the common hymnal text. Tune HANKEY (W. G. Fischer, 1869), meter and composer per hymnary.org/tune/hankey_fischer, which lists A-flat and G as the usual printed keys; G chosen as the nearest guitar key. Chart derived from the Cyber Hymnal's own MIDI of HANKEY (mid/h/a/n/k/hankey.mid) transposed A-flat->G, then reduced to one or two changes per bar; short passing chords (a Ddim and a half-beat A7 in stanza line 1) were dropped as unplayable noise on a strummed instrument.
